stem: The box plots summarize the scores of the 24 students in Class A and the 24 students in Class B on the same test. Approximately how many more students in Class B than in Class A scored at least 70?
solution: In Class A, 70 is the median, so about half of the 24 students, 12, scored at least 70.
In Class B, 70 is the first quartile, so about three quarters of the 24 students, 18, scored at least 70.

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the difference between the medians, \(78 - 70\), not a difference in numbers of students.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the number of students in Class A who scored at least 70, not the difference between the classes.
explanation.C: Correct. About 18 students in Class B and 12 in Class A scored at least 70, a difference of 6.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the number of students in Class B who scored at least 70, not how many more than in Class A.

verify:
P = {p['name']: p for p in figure['plots']}
assert P['Class A']['median'] == 70 and P['Class B']['q1'] == 70
a = Rational(24, 2)
b = Rational(3 * 24, 4)
d = b - a
assert d == 6
assert value(choices[answer]) == d
assert all(value(choices[k]) != d for k in choices if k != answer)

checks.note: Approximate read from box plots; answer depends on estimating counts.
